# Topics

This folder serves as the central knowledge base for the clinical management, quality assurance, and epidemiological tracking of atrial fibrillation within the Danish healthcare system, primarily anchored by the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database (AFDK). It groups specialized areas covering national quality indicators, clinical guidelines, patient outcomes, and pharmacovigilance, alongside the rigorous methodological definitions, coding specifications, and data infrastructure required to maintain registry integrity. Additionally, it documents the organizational structures, policy decisions, and geographic performance trends that shape cardiovascular care delivery and quality improvement initiatives across Denmark's regions and hospitals.

## Pages

- [[topics/clinical-guideline/index|Clinical Guideline]] — Details the clinical policies for atrial fibrillation management, including pharmacological interventions, CHA2DS2-VASc thresholds, and structured patient education programs.
- [[topics/clinical-indicators/index|Clinical Indicators]] — Groups the clinical quality indicators and performance benchmarks used to monitor cardiovascular care, including diagnostic compliance, adverse outcomes, and condition-specific safety metrics.
- [[topics/clinical-outcome/index|Clinical Outcome]] — Tracks clinical outcomes and adverse events for atrial fibrillation patients, including severe bleeding, ischemic stroke, and supplementary mortality indicators.
- [[topics/clinical-practice/index|Clinical Practice]] — Covers the clinical management of atrial fibrillation in Denmark, focusing on anticoagulation initiation, regional variations, and structured patient education programs.
- [[topics/clinical-practice-decision/index|Clinical Practice Decision]] — Details operational and systemic choices in the Danish healthcare system, such as emergency pathways and standardized patient education interventions.

- [[topics/clinical-risk-distribution/index|Clinical Risk Distribution]] — Explores the real-world distribution of risk scores and their predictive limitations, highlighting the paradox of severe bleeding in low-risk cohorts.
- [[topics/clinical-tools/index|Clinical Tools]] — Groups theoretical frameworks and structured care models, including the CARE model and risk assessment tools like the ABC Pathway.

- [[topics/definition/index|Definition]] — Outlines the AFDK's standardized criteria for patient populations, clinical quality indicator calculations, and secondary outcomes like heart failure.

- [[topics/epidemiology/index|Epidemiology]] — Documents the epidemiological profile of atrial fibrillation in Denmark, synthesizing national registry data on incidence, prevalence, and associated cardiovascular complications.
